Regular dodecahedron :: Other related geometric objects :: chunk_0006
The regular dodecahedron can be interpreted as the [Goldberg polyhedron](/wiki/Goldberg_polyhedron "Goldberg polyhedron"). It is a set of polyhedra containing hexagonal and pentagonal faces. Other than two Platonic solids—tetrahedron and cube—the regular dodecahedron is the initial of the Goldberg polyhedron construction, and the next polyhedron is obtained by truncating all of its edges, a process called [chamfer](/wiki/Chamfer_(geometry) "Chamfer (geometry)"). This process can be continuously repeated, resulting in more new Goldberg's polyhedra. These polyhedra are classified as the first class of a Goldberg polyhedron.[[23]](#cite_note-hart-23)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Small_stellated_dodecahedron_constructed_by_dodecahedron.svg/250px-Small_stellated_dodecahedron_constructed_by_dodecahedron.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Small_stellated_dodecahedron_constructed_by_dodecahedron.svg)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Trapezohedron5.jpg/250px-Trapezohedron5.jpg)](/wiki/File:Trapezohedron5.jpg)

[Small stellated dodecahedron](/wiki/Small_stellated_dodecahedron "Small stellated dodecahedron") and [trapezohedron](/wiki/Trapezohedron "Trapezohedron")

The [stellations](/wiki/Stellation "Stellation") of the regular dodecahedron make up three of the four [Kepler–Poinsot polyhedra](/wiki/Kepler%E2%80%93Poinsot_polyhedra "Kepler–Poinsot polyhedra"). The first stellation of a regular dodecahedron is constructed by attaching its layer with pentagonal pyramids, forming a [small stellated dodecahedron](/wiki/Small_stellated_dodecahedron "Small stellated dodecahedron"). The second stellation is by attaching the small stellated dodecahedron with [wedges](/wiki/Wedge_(geometry) "Wedge (geometry)"), forming a [great dodecahedron](/wiki/Great_dodecahedron "Great dodecahedron"). The third stellation is by attaching the great dodecahedron with the sharp triangular pyramids, forming a [great stellated dodecahedron](/wiki/Great_stellated_dodecahedron "Great stellated dodecahedron").[[24]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECromwell1997[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidOJowej1QWpoCpgPA265_26

The major topographic features of the Saharan region

The Sahara comprises several distinct [ecoregions](/wiki/Ecoregion "Ecoregion"). With their variations in temperature, rainfall, elevation, and soil, these regions harbor distinct communities of plants and animals.

* The [Atlantic coastal desert](/wiki/Atlantic_coastal_desert "Atlantic coastal desert") is a narrow strip along the Atlantic coast where fog generated offshore by the cool [Canary Current](/wiki/Canary_Current "Canary Current") provides sufficient moisture to sustain a variety of [lichens](/wiki/Lichen "Lichen"), [succulents](/wiki/Succulent_plant "Succulent plant"), and shrubs. It covers an area of 39,900 square kilometers (15,400 sq mi) in the south of Morocco and Mauritania.[[44]](#cite_note-44)
* The [North Saharan steppe and woodlands](/wiki/North_Saharan_steppe_and_woodlands "North Saharan steppe and woodlands") is along the northern desert, next to the [Mediterranean forests, woodlands, and scrub](/wiki/Mediterranean_forests,_woodlands,_and_scrub "Mediterranean forests, woodlands, and scrub") ecoregions of the northern Maghreb and Cyrenaica. Winter rains sustain shrublands and dry woodlands that form a transition between the Mediterranean climate regions to the north and the hyper-arid Sahara proper to the south. It covers 1,675,300 square kilometers (646,840 sq mi) in Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, and Tunisia.[[45]](#cite_note-45)
* The [Sahara desert ecoregion](/wiki/Sahara_desert_(ecoregion) "Sahara desert (ecoregion)") covers the hyper-arid central portion of the Sahara where rainfall is minimal and sporadic. Vegetation is rare, and this ecoregion consists mostly of sand dunes (*erg, chech, raoui*), stone plateaus (*hamadas*), gravel plains (*reg*), dry valleys (*wadis*), and salt flats. All types of [alcoholic beverages](/wiki/Alcoholic_beverage "Alcoholic beverage"), including beer, wine, or liquor, cause breast cancer.

Drinking [alcoholic beverages](/wiki/Alcoholic_beverage "Alcoholic beverage") increases the risk of breast cancer, even among very light drinkers (women drinking less than half of one alcoholic drink per day).[[104]](#cite_note-Choi-104) The risk is highest among heavy drinkers.[[105]](#cite_note-Shield-105) Globally, about one in ten cases of breast cancer is caused by women drinking alcoholic beverages.[[105]](#cite_note-Shield-105) Alcohol use is among the most common modifiable risk factors.[[106]](#cite_note-106)

[Obesity](/wiki/Obesity "Obesity") and [diabetes](/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes") increase the risk of breast cancer. A high [body mass index](/wiki/Body_mass_index "Body mass index") (BMI) causes 7% of breast cancers; diabetes mellitus is responsible for 2%.[[107]](#cite_note-NIHR_Evidence_2023-107)[[108]](#cite_note-108) At the same time, the correlation between obesity and breast cancer is not at all linear. Studies show that those who rapidly gain weight in adulthood are at higher risk than those who have been overweight since childhood. Likewise, excess fat in the [midriff](/wiki/Midriff "Midriff") seems to induce a higher risk than excess weight carried in the lower body.[[109]](#cite_note-109) Dietary factors that may increase risk include a high-fat diet[[110]](#cite_note-110) and obesity-related [high cholesterol](/wiki/High_cholesterol "High cholesterol") levels.[[111]](#cite_note-111)[[112]](#cite_note-112)

After a rough cut was shown at [2004 Toronto International Film Festival](/wiki/2004_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2004 Toronto International Film Festival"), the film premiered at the Elgin Theatre in [Toronto](/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") in September 2004. It was quickly purchased by [Lions Gate Films](/wiki/Lions_Gate_Films "Lions Gate Films") for $3.5 million.[[7]](#cite_note-Wright-7)[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10) *Crash* had a [wide release](/wiki/Wide_release "Wide release") on May 6, 2005, and was a box office success in the late spring of 2005.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

The film grossed $53.4 million domestically, making back more than seven times its estimated $6.5 million-budget.[[1]](#cite_note-BOM-1) Despite its success in relation to its cost, *Crash* was the lowest-grossing film at the domestic box office to win [Best Picture](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") since *[The Last Emperor](/wiki/The_Last_Emperor "The Last Emperor")* in 1987.[[19]](#cite_note-19)
